title: Microsoft Teams: users can report a security concern in meetings
summary: The briefing needs one correction before publication: it says reports reach Defender if nobody acts, but existing tenants must enable Defender monitoring for reports to appear correctly. The documented controls, licensing, default-on reporting and rollout dates are otherwise supported.

claims.claim: Microsoft names Allow users to report meetings but has not published a selectable navigation path to that Teams admin center policy.
claims.quote: Searched: "Allow users to report meetings" Teams admin center navigation ReportMeeting; opened meeting reporting and Teams user reporting; read quick-configure excerpts. The route says only "open the policy or settings page that controls reporting for Teams meetings".

claims.claim: Set-CsTeamsMeetingConfiguration -Identity Global -ReportMeeting Enabled|Disabled controls meeting reporting options tenant-wide.
claims.quote: Controls whether end users can access the "Report a concern" and "Report as not a concern" options in the meeting experience (including meeting UI and meeting chat). ... Possible values: Enabled; Disabled. ... The only valid input is Global

claims.claim: Learn does not explicitly identify ReportMeeting as the same setting as Allow users to report meetings.
claims.quote: Searched: "ReportMeeting" "Allow users to report meetings"; opened Set-CsTeamsMeetingConfiguration, meeting reporting and Teams user reporting. Both controls are described, but no passage explicitly equates their setting names.

claims.claim: Meeting and participant reports follow the same Teams user reported destination settings despite the PowerShell parameters' chat-message names.
claims.quote: When users report Teams messages or calls or report meetings or meeting participants as malicious or non malicious, the reported items are sent to Microsoft and/or the reporting mailbox as defined by the Teams user reported settings in Defender for Office 365.

claims.claim: Monitoring is at Microsoft Defender portal > Settings > Email & collaboration > Teams user reported settings tab > Microsoft Teams > Monitor reported items in Microsoft Teams.
claims.quote: go to Settings > Email & collaboration > Teams user reported settings tab. ... On the Teams user reported settings page, go to the Microsoft Teams section for the Monitor reported items in Microsoft Teams setting.

claims.claim: No documented automation specifically changes the Defender Monitor reported items in Microsoft Teams control.
claims.quote: Searched: "Monitor reported items in Microsoft Teams" PowerShell enable disable; Graph Teams reported meeting submissions API Monitor reported items; opened Teams user reporting and searched Set-ReportSubmissionPolicy. Destination parameters are documented, not this monitoring toggle.

claims.claim: Administrators review submissions at Microsoft Defender portal > Actions & submissions > Submissions > User reported tab.
claims.quote: In the Microsoft Defender portal at https://security.microsoft.com, go to Actions & submissions > Submissions. ... On the Submissions page, select the User reported tab.

claims.claim: No documented API retrieves the reported meeting submissions shown in Defender.
claims.quote: Searched: "Microsoft Graph" "meeting" "user reported" submissions API; Graph security threatSubmission Teams meeting submissions beta. Opened Submissions and Teams SecOps pages; read threatSubmission reference excerpts for email, URL and file threats. None documented meeting submissions.

claims.claim: Meeting submission details are also accessible through View submission in the Defender XDR incident.
claims.quote: SecOps team members can review submitted Teams message, call, meeting, or meeting participant details in the following locations in the Defender portal: The View submission action in the Defender XDR incident.

claims.claim: Alert policies are at Microsoft Defender portal > Email & collaboration > Policies & rules > Alert policy.
claims.quote: To view and create alert policies, in the Microsoft Defender portal, under Email & collaboration select Policies & rules > Alert policy.

claims.claim: No supported command for modifying the built-in reported-call alert policies was established.
claims.quote: Searched: Set-ProtectionAlert built-in default alert policies Teams reported call update PowerShell; opened Alert policies and read Set-ProtectionAlert reference excerpts: "You can't use this cmdlet to edit default alert policies." No alternative operation was returned.

claims.claim: Manage Alerts is required to create and edit alert policies.
claims.quote: You have to be assigned the Manage Alerts role to create and edit alert policies.

claims.claim: Built-in alert policies can be turned off or on.
claims.quote: You can turn off these policies (or back on again), set up a list of recipients to send email notifications to, and set a daily notification limit. The other settings for these policies can't be edited.

claims.claim: The Teams report is at Teams admin center > Analytics & reports > Protection reports > View reports tab > Report > User reported security submissions.
claims.quote: In the left navigation of the Teams admin center, go to Analytics & reports > Protection reports. On the View reports tab, under Report, select User reported security submissions.

claims.claim: An API for the Teams admin center User reported security submissions report is not documented.
claims.quote: Searched: "User reported security submissions" API Graph export; opened the Teams security submissions report page. It documents viewing and CSV export; search returned that page and unrelated email/eDiscovery reports, not an API for this report.

claims.claim: The Teams report page lists Calling, Chats and channels, and User, but no meetings category.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams meeting reporting Teams admin center User reported security submissions; opened the security submissions report page. Its Report category choices are Calling, Chats and channels, User; no meeting category is documented.

claims.claim: The printed Microsoft-only Set-ReportSubmissionPolicy call is documented with ReportChatMessageEnabled true, ReportChatMessageToCustomizedAddressEnabled false and EnableUserEmailNotification true.
claims.quote: Set-ReportSubmissionPolicy -Identity DefaultReportSubmissionPolicy -ReportChatMessageEnabled $true -ReportChatMessageToCustomizedAddressEnabled $false -EnableUserEmailNotification $true

claims.claim: The Teams setting controls whether users can report meeting concerns.
claims.quote: In the Teams admin center: Controls whether users are able to report items from Teams. When the applicable setting is turned off, users can't report those items within Teams, so the corresponding setting in the Microsoft Defender portal is irrelevant.

claims.claim: If nobody acts, reports land in the Defender portal and Teams admin center.
claims.quote: In the Microsoft Defender portal: On by default for new tenants. Existing tenants need to enable it. ... it also needs to be turned on in the Defender portal for user reported items to show up correctly on the User reported tab on the Submissions page.
claims.fix: Replace 'If nobody acts, reports land in the Defender portal and Teams admin center with no agreed owner' with 'Existing tenants need to enable Defender monitoring for submitted reports to show correctly on the User reported tab; without preparation'. Keep the remaining warning about missing user guidance and copying metadata when Microsoft is a destination. This carries the monitoring qualification stated at https://learn.microsoft.com/defender-office-365/submissions-teams.
